messages:
maria: Kicking off thread — saw a weird formatting bleed when we ran INT8 + 50% structured prune on model-x today. tables got mashed, numbers concatenated.
jamal: Ugh. Quick question: does this happen only with prune enabled or also with unpruned INT8?
maria: Unpruned INT8 looks mostly fine, small EM drops. The prune+int8 combo is the one that spikes hallucination on table->text tasks.
ken: Can you paste a short example of the bad output? :eyes:
maria: Sure — original prompt -> expected table rows -> text summary.
maria: Bad output snippet:
```
Row1: user_id=1234amount$5000Row2:user_id=1235amount$6000
```
maria: Notice missing whitespace/newline boundaries and numeric glue.
ciara: That looks like tokenization alignment shift in generation. Could be KV cache pointer offsets after pruning changed layer shapes.
eval-bot: Automated eval summary for run 1854321111-runA:
```
tasks: [table2text, qa-short, formatting]
baseline (fp16): table2text EM: 82.1%, halluc: 1.2%
int8 (no prune): table2text EM: 80.9%, halluc: 1.8%
int8 + prune50: table2text EM: 73.4%, halluc: 13.5%
```
jamal: Whoa, halluc rate x7 vs baseline for prune combo. That's huge.
ken: Important to note: other tasks (qa-short) only show small dips, looks task-specific to structured outputs.
ciara: Hypotheses: 1) pruning changes attention head indexing -> token alignment shift 2) quantization noise amplifies small misalignments 3) calibration dataset mismatch for prune config.
maria: I ran a quick ablation: int8+prune but with longer calibration set (10k vs 1k) — halluc decreased to ~8.2% but EM still down ~5 points.
jamal: So calibration helps but doesn't fully recover. Can we test disable KV cache optimizations as a sanity check?
ken: Proposal for bisect plan:
- run int8 (no prune) baseline
- run int8 + prune50 (current)
- run int8 + prune50 without KV-cache opt
- run int8 + prune50 with per-layer calibration
- run fp16 + prune50
also try different pruning pattern (magnitude vs structured block)
ciara: Add: test padding/sequence length edge cases — table2text uses many short rows which might interact with prefix caching.
maria: I can queue those overnight. Also opening a small eval set of 200 focused table prompts to replicate quickly.
jamal: If this reproduces, we should mark prune50 as not deployable for table-heavy routes and fallback to int8 or fp16 until we find fix. Flag in deployment profile.
ken: Agreed. Add route rule: if model variant == int8+prune50 && route in {table2text, report-gen} -> fallback to int8.
ciara: One more debug: dump attention maps for a failing example pre/post prune to see head shifts.
eval-bot: Added job 1854321111-aux to CI queue: "int8-prune50-bisect". Will post results when done.
maria: Thanks. Will post first 20 diffs when job finishes. @ken @ciara @jamal please react if you want early access to logs.
ken: :thumbsup:
ciara: :face_with_monocle:
jamal: Adding to the incident tracker as a model-regression candidate.
maria: Filing a short notes doc in confluence after first repro. For now, blocking prune50 promotion for prod table routes.
